paper_metadata.title: A 100-MS/s 8-b CMOS Subranging ADC with Sustained Parametric Performance from 3.8 V Down to 2.2 V
paper_metadata.abstract: A 100-MS/s 8-b CMOS analog-to-digital converter (ADC) designed for very low supply voltage and power dissipation is presented. This single-ended-input ADC is based on the unified two-step subranging architecture, which processes the coarse and fine decisions in identical signal paths to maximize their matching. However, to minimize power and area, the coarse-to-fine overlap correction has been aggressively reduced to only one LSB. The ADC incorporates five established design techniques to maximize performance: bottom-plate sampling, distributed sampling, autozeroing, interpolation, and interleaving. Very low voltage operation required for a general purpose ADC was obtained with four additional and new circuit techniques. These are a dual-gain first-stage amplifier, differential T-gate boosting, a supply independent delay generator, and a digital delay-locked-loop controlled output driver.
